coverage_note: S 86, where the functional problems are identified with the problems of constitution, and SS 150-153, the closing chapter in which constitution is stratified, transferred to all regions and finally extended to the whole of phenomenology. The intervening noetic-noematic analyses (SS 87-148) carry the term hardly at all - many of the longest sections in the commentary contain no term of the family - and two of them are recorded as absences.

units.claim: The very greatest problems are the functional problems, those of the constitution of the consciousness-objectivities.
units.quote: But the very greatest problems are the functional problems, or those of the "constitution of the consciousness-objectivities."

units.claim: The central problem of all phenomenology is how objectivity is constituted in and for consciousness through the manifold of consciousness.
units.quote: This is the central problem of all phenomenology: how objectivity is constituted in and for consciousness.

units.claim: The region thing serves as the transcendental guiding-thread for the constitutive analysis.
units.quote: So the region thing is the transcendental leitfaden (guiding-thread) for the constitutive analysis.

units.claim: The constitutive analysis requires the reflective turn from the object to the constituting consciousness, and these reflections open the research-field of the constitution of the thing.
units.quote: These reflections are it that now open us a great, in itself connected research-field, or a mighty, under the Idea thing-region standing problematic.

units.claim: Every stage and every stratum of the thing-constitution constitutes an own unity which is a necessary middle-member for the full constitution of the thing.
units.quote: Every stage and every stratum in the stage is characterized thereby, that it constitutes an own unity, which on its side is necessary middle-member for the full constitution of the thing.

units.claim: The lowest stage constitutes the thing for one ego, culminating in the substantial-causal thing, which is still bound to one experiencing subject and its perception-manifolds.
units.quote: So the lowest stage constitutes the thing for one ego, culminating in the substantial-causal thing (still subject-relative).

units.claim: The next-higher stage is the intersubjectively identical thing, a constitutive unity of higher order whose constitution is related to an open plurality of subjects in mutual understanding.
units.quote: The next-higher stage is then the intersubjectively-identical thing, a constitutive unity of higher order. Its constitution is related to an open plurality of subjects standing in the relation of "mutual understanding"

units.claim: Empathy is asked after for the constituting role it plays in objective experience, giving unity to the perception-manifolds of separate ego-subjects.
units.quote: above all, however, to the new of the empathy and the question, how it in the "objective" experience plays a constituting role and gives those separated manifolds unity.

units.claim: What was said exemplarily of the constitution of the material thing must transfer to all object-regions according to problem and to method.
units.quote: One sees without further that what here exemplarily for the constitution of the material thing was said — namely with respect to the constitution in the system of the manifolds of the before all "thinking" lying experience — must transfer to all object-regions, according to problem and according to method.

units.claim: The constitution-problems concern the principial of all the material sciences, each grounded in its regional ontology and that in its constitution.
units.quote: The constitution-problems concern the **principial** (the foundations) of all material sciences — what groups around the regional Ideas (the fundamental concepts and cognitions, unfolded in the regional ontologies). So phenomenology grounds the principial (foundations) of all the material sciences (each grounded in its regional ontology, which is grounded in its constitution).

units.claim: Suitably extended to the formal sphere, the Idea of constitution finally encompasses the whole of phenomenology, so that all of phenomenology is constitutive phenomenology.
units.quote: So, suitably extended, the Idea of constitution finally **encompasses the whole of phenomenology**. So all of phenomenology is constitutive phenomenology (the constitution of all objectivities, material and formal).

absences.expected_because: Intentionality is named the principal phenomenological theme two sections before S 86 identifies the functional problems with the problems of constitution. The section states the theme without any term of the family.
The noema is introduced here, and it is the noema that SS 150-151 make the correlate of thing-constitution. The introduction of the term carries no vocabulary of constitution at all.
